answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 23% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the hostile operator's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the bridge reward in the ocean ledger costs the operator directly, and the dawn audit records each payout. A farm of 237 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the swarm makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
